findings.body:
Removing `ALLOWED_HOSTS` and the `urlsplit` check means `deliver()` will POST to any `url` passed in. With customer-configured endpoints, that is SSRF: a malicious or compromised tenant URL can target `http://127.0.0.1`, `http://169.254.169.254/` (cloud metadata), or internal hostnames. `urlopen` also follows redirects by default, so a seemingly public URL can chain into the private network.

Restore a server-side URL policy before `Request`/`urlopen` — for example HTTPS-only, resolve and reject loopback/link-local/private ranges, limit redirects, and/or keep a per-tenant allowlist. Do not ship open egress solely on the comment that customer endpoints are desired.

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — this change removes the only webhook host allowlist and posts to an attacker-influenced URL with no replacement controls.

## Analysis

`deliver()` previously rejected any host outside `ALLOWED_HOSTS` (`hooks.internal.example`) before building the request. The PR deletes that gate and calls `urllib.request.urlopen` on the raw `url` argument.

If `url` is customer- or user-controlled (the PR description says it is), this is classic SSRF: the runner/server can be steered at link-local metadata (`169.254.169.254`), loopback, RFC1918 addresses, or internal hostnames. `urllib.request` follows redirects by default, so a public HTTPS endpoint can still bounce into the internal network unless redirect and address checks are explicit.

Supporting customer endpoints is a valid product goal; it needs an allowlist/denylist or equivalent URL policy (scheme HTTPS-only, block private/link-local/metadata ranges after DNS resolution, cap redirects, optional per-tenant allowlist) — not an unconditional open egress.

## Release decision

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: Base `deliver()` enforced `ALLOWED_HOSTS` via `urlsplit` before `urlopen`; head removes that guard and POSTs to any caller-supplied `url`, enabling SSRF (including redirect chains). Claimed critical severity matches open egress to internal/metadata targets.
